Hi Melanie —

Sorry about the friction. Quick context: Google Meet will sometimes enforce organizer domain restrictions when the event was created by a calendar proxy or when an organizer field gets set to a forwarded address. Two short options that are lowest risk:

- Option A (recommended): We send a fresh invite with a Zoom meeting (one-click join) — I can create the Zoom and Jonas will send the calendar item from his account so the organizer matches.
- Option B: We re-issue the Google Meet invite but explicitly transfer organizer rights to Jonas (requires CloudSpring admin to accept organizer claim) — this can be slower depending on your admin SLA.

If you prefer Zoom I’ll create the meeting and attach a new .ics. If you want to keep Meet, we can open an admin ticket but I’d rather avoid that if the demo is time-sensitive.

Proposed immediate action: Jonas — can you send a replacement invite from your calendar and include the Zoom link below? I created the meeting id and pasted it into zoom-alt-link.txt (attached).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.inference
